messages:
aya: hitting intermittent 429s for a customer this morning. bursts come from a single NAT IP but with multiple API keys. sometimes the 429s show up as org-level, other times as project-level. can repro locally but need eyes on scoping logic.

maria: any deploys to the rate/attrib service in the last 24h?

aya: not from my side. customer pattern: proxy rotates Authorization header per request but preserves X-Forwarded-For. they run parallel clients.

todd: i pulled traces — interesting. gateway does quick ip->bucket resolve before token validation completes. ordering can flip depending on auth cache hit. snippet from auth logs: 
```
[2026-06-01T09:12:13Z] resolve_scopes: seen=[ip:35.190.23.1, key:proj-A] validation_time_ms=180 final_scope=ip:35.190.23.1
[2026-06-01T09:12:13Z] resolve_scopes: seen=[key:proj-B, ip:35.190.23.1] validation_time_ms=40 final_scope=key:proj-B
```

maria: that matches a race where ip attribution wins if token validation > threshold. could be cache miss on token introspection.

aya: repro script I used (redacted keys):
```
for i in {1..250}; do
  (curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $((i%2==0?\"sk-proj-A\":\"sk-proj-B\"))" \
    -H "X-Forwarded-For: 35.190.23.1" \
    -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' &)
done; wait
```

aya: result: ~12% 429s. in the request logs some 429s attribute to org:acme (org-level quota), others to proj-A/B. customer sees org quota exhausted even though keys should be charging to projects.

todd: mitigation options:
- short-term: ask customer to pin X-Project-ID header or use per-project dedicated key so token validation hits cache faster.
- medium-term: make scoping deterministic: prefer validated token scope over IP when both present, or require token validation before final attribution.

maria: for immediate triage we can limit the NAT IP bucket to reduce blast radius while we patch attribution. create escalation with request ids and sample traces.

aya: done, escalation created with customer request ids and the repro script. attaching two sample request_ids: req_20260601_aa12, req_20260601_bb34.

sre-bot: incident INC-2026-234 opened by @maria. paging oncall. :rotating_light:

todd: quick log extract showing tiebreaker metric: 
```
metric:attribution_latency{step="token_validation"} 0.18
metric:attribution_latency{step="ip_lookup"} 0.02
```

maria: nice. i'll add this to the ticket and note that token cache warmup is a likely root cause. also adding a short-run mitigation to prefer Authorization header if validation completes within 200ms.

aya: update from customer after we asked them to set X-Project-ID header: zero 429s for 35 minutes. they can keep doing that as a workaround. :tada:

todd: follow-up action items:
- engineering: change attribution ordering to be deterministic (auth first if present and validated within threshold). owner: @todd.
- platform: add a telemetry flag to surface attribution_source per request in console. owner: @maria.
- support: keep customer informed and remove IP throttling after patch. owner: @aya.

maria: i'll open a PR with tests that simulate token cache miss/warm paths.

aya: adding repro steps and the curl script to the escalation ticket. will confirm when customer re-tests post-patch.

sre-bot: INC-2026-234 status: investigating -> mitigation applied (IP temporary limit).
